newsitem.title: USA: Emerson Electric results up on international demand.
newsitem.headline: Emerson Electric results up on international demand.

text.p: Emerson Electric Co. Tuesday reported higher third-quarter sales and earnings, based on the strength of international demand for its electronics products.
The St. Louis-based company had earnings for the quarter ended June 30 of $296.6 million, or 67 cents per share, up from $266.9 million, or 60 cents per share a year earlier.
Sales rose 10.8 percent to $3.21 billion from $2.89 billion over the same period.
The results reflect strong international and modest domestic demand, as well as the impact of acquisitions, said Charles Knight, chairman and chief executive officer.
"All of our businesses reported underlying sales growth this quarter," he said in a statement.

"Excluding the negative impact of currency, strong underlying international sales were achieved through robust export sales and continued strength in faster growth regions such as Asia-Pacific and Latin America," he said.
The underlying electronics business continued its very strong performance due, in part, to new products and strength in both domestic and international markets, Emerson said.

The process business saw rising U.S. demand and strong international sales growth that were partially offset by negative currency translation. The underlying tools business achieved solid sales growth as domestic demand grew.
Emerson Electric stock fell 62.5 cents to $58.625 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
